subject: Follow-up: competitive perf eval & latency test plan with ClearApps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Caroline Nguyen <caroline@clearapps.ai>, Ali Hassan <ali.h@enterprise-tech.com>
Date: 2026-04-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + ask: perf A/B plan for ClearApps POC

Thanks again to Caroline and Ali for the call earlier — good discussion. Quick internal recap and request for a concrete A/B plan we can share with the ClearApps engineers.

Key points from the call:
- Customer goal: replace current hyperscaler endpoint (HCloud text-13b) for their chat agent to cut per-token cost ~25% while improving 95th/99th latency (p95 target <= 220ms, p99 <= 400ms).
- Typical prompt mix: 60% short queries (~30 tokens), 30% medium (~150 tokens), 10% long (~800 tokens).
- Expected concurrency: bursty, sustained concurrency 40-80 qps during peak.
- Success criteria: p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec sustained, and answer-quality parity on our prompt set.

Ask: please draft a runnable A/B benchmark plan (metrics, scripts, dataset, infra config) we can commit to next-week test window. Rachel on their infra team will provide service keys and a shortlist of 200 test prompts.

Priority items for the plan:
- Clear definitions for p95/p99 and how we warm cache/steady-state measurement
- Configs for batching, KV-cache on/off, and quantization variants to test
- Exact commands + expected output format so ClearApps can run and share logs
- Timeline to run two rounds (initial smoke + full run) and a Slack/Zoom check-in

I attached the customer-provided sample prompts (placeholder — final set will come from Rachel).

Thanks — J

--
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Caroline Nguyen <caroline@clearapps.ai>, Ali Hassan <ali.h@enterprise-tech.com>
Date: 2026-04-11T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick recap + ask: perf A/B plan for ClearApps POC

Jasmine — see below a concrete plan we can hand to ClearApps. I kept commands curl-friendly and included metrics we’ll capture.

High-level plan (2-stage):
1) Smoke test (30 min): 100 prompts, concurrency ramp 1 -> 20, single seed run per config. Purpose: verify connectivity, auth, and baseline latency.
2) Full run (2 hours): 2k prompts randomized, steady-state 60 qps target, multiple repeats (3 runs per config) to get distribution.

Configs to test (A/B matrix):
- A1 (Redwood): rwd-13b-int8 + Redwood runtime with KV-cache enabled, batch_size=8, concurrency=60, GPU: A100-80GB; quant profile "q8_steady"
- A2 (Redwood): rwd-13b-fp16 + KV-cache disabled, batch_size=1, concurrency=40, to compare cold-start behavior
- B  (Hyperscaler baseline): HCloud-text-13b default endpoint, concurrency=60, no server-side batching (customer's current config)

Metrics captured (per-request and aggregated):
- request_id, start_ts, end_ts, total_tokens_in, total_tokens_out, server_token_time_ms, client_roundtrip_ms
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (client roundtrip), tokens/sec per-second series, throughput (tokens/sec) for steady-state window (last 60 min bucket)
- CPU/GPU utilization (if ClearApps can provide), error rates, 5xx/4xx counts

Measurement details:
- Warm-up: run 200 requests at low concurrency before each config to populate KV cache.
- Steady-state window: measure metrics during 15-30 minute window after warm-up where tokens/sec and latency stabilize.
- p95/p99 calculation: compute from client roundtrip_ms excluding the initial warm-up period; report both raw and folded by prompt length bucket (short/med/long).

Sample curl harness (simplified):
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-13b-int8","input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":256,"stream":false}' 
  | jq -rc '{request_id: .id, latency_ms: (.meta.client_ms), tokens_out: .usage.total_tokens}' >> results.ndjson

Output format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with the fields above so we can compute p95/p99 and tokens/sec easily. I attached a starter matrix CSV with columns for config, batch_size, concurrency, quant_profile: redwood_bench_matrix.csv

Proposed schedule:
- Wed 2026-04-14 10:00-12:30 PT: smoke + full run (Redwood team on standby for logs)
- Thurs 2026-04-15 09:00 PT: quick debrief with ClearApps to review preliminary p95/p99 and tokens/sec plots

I'll also enable tracing hooks in the Redwood runtime so we can correlate per-token kernel time if we need to dig deeper.

Let me know if that schedule works. I can drop a minimal k6/locust harness for them if they want a reproducible runner.

-Logan

Attachments referenced: redwood_bench_matrix.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Caroline Nguyen <caroline@clearapps.ai>, Ali Hassan <ali.h@enterprise-tech.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick recap + ask: perf A/B plan for ClearApps POC

Couple product notes to add into the plan so the comparison is apples-to-apples: 

1) Quantization and model variants: When testing rwd-13b-int8 vs fp16 we should call out that int8 is tuned for throughput and might introduce tiny output drift. Include a quality check step that runs 200 prompts and computes BLEU/ROUGE and a small human-sample check for hallucination.

2) Fallback behavior: include a test iteration where we intentionally throttle capacity to observe graceful degradation — e.g., route to a smaller variant (rwd-6b) and measure p95/p99 change and cost delta. This is one of our differentiators vs major hyperscalers.

3) Observability hooks: please ensure ClearApps enables X-Request-ID in their client so we can stitch logs. We'll export: per-token timing series (if available), model variant tag, kernel/quant profile, and batch size. If they can't provide GPU telemetry, we'll rely on per-request timings and our tracing.

4) Success gating: beyond latency targets, require parity on the prompt-set quality metrics (no more than 3% regression in correctness on the sampled QA prompts).

I'll prepare a short one-pager summarizing differences to send to their leadership after the run (cost/perf/quality).

-marissa

From: Caroline Nguyen <caroline@clearapps.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-13T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick recap + ask: perf A/B plan for ClearApps POC

Thanks, all — this looks good and covers the concerns we raised. A couple of clarifications from our side before Wed: 

- We prefer starting with a smaller sample (500 prompts) for the full run and then scale to 2k if the smoke looks clean. Can we do the 500-first approach?
- For secure transfer of our prompt-set and test keys we'll use our S3 pre-signed links and a short-lived service account — I'll have Rachel send the link by end-of-day tomorrow.
- Our p99 target is 450ms for the short/med buckets; above that we want to understand root cause.

Ali (cc'd) will own running the harness from our side. We're good with the Wed AM PT start window; please send the run command and the ndjson schema so our infra can validate outputs.

— Caroline

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>

3) Deliverables we’ll provide before the run:

Attachments: clearapps_promptset_v1.txt, redwood_bench_matrix.csv

See you Wed — Jasmine
